query:
The group operates with an expectation that everyone contributes something — food or a game — to shared sessions and events. Based on the conversations, does this expectation apply to every member? If not, who approaches it differently and what does the conversation show about their actual practice?

Options:
A. Nadia
B. Soo-Yeon
C. Raj
D. Marcus
context:
[1] (about=Lena, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:05:00) so basically the norm here is bring something, game or food, agreed tbh. one could argue that even the people who brought nothing last year understood this expectation, they just didn't follow through
[2] (about=Marcus, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:03:00) The rule is bring a game or bring food. Both is ideal. Enforcement is just social pressure.
[3] (about=Nadia, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:06:00) I will bring a game. I do not participate in the food arrangement.
[4] (about=Priya, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:02:00) love that. also we need to talk about the bring-something rule. last year two people showed up empty-handed, no snacks no game nothing 😅
[5] (about=Marcus, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:18:00) Everyone pitches on the day. Priya has the format.
[6] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:04:00) In my experience the marathon only works when everyone contributes. It is the social contract of a shared day.
[7] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t0 @2026-03-02T19:11:00) Oath has a learning curve that would eat the whole evening. In my experience, new members need something with a shorter rules overhead first. Perhaps we revisit it when everyone has a baseline.
[8] (about=Lena, episodic, t0 @2026-03-02T19:18:00) so basically the themed snack thing is actually a nice warm-up ritual tbh, it sets the tone before the game even starts. one could argue it's part of the social contract of game night
[9] (about=Lena, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:24:00) Priya you mentioned a relational disclosure earlier that I wanted to follow up on tbh. you and Derek seem to have different vibes about the session energy. like i've noticed he tends to go quiet when cooperative options are even mentioned?
[10] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t2 @2026-04-06T19:01:00) Pierogi are on the stove. Game is Viticulture. In my experience it is a good socialiser since turns are long enough for conversation but short enough to stay engaged.
[11] (about=GROUP, said_by=Lena, group-insight, t14 @2026-04-20T19:01:00) The norm is that everyone brings something (game or food) to the marathon; even those who brought nothing last year understood the expectation but didn't follow through.
[12] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t14 @2026-04-20T19:01:00) Confirmed participation in the marathon; everyone brings pitches and snacks.
[13] (about=Soo-Yeon, core, t2 @2026-04-06T19:00:00) Willing to try Fuse as a warm-up, finding cooperative real-time less intimidating than solo speed; after playing, notes team communication absorbed most of the pressure and unexpectedly enjoyed it.
